title: Rumors
summary: Rumors for the tavern, some true and some not. A few only come up when a story tag or the time of day fits.

tables.name: Rumor
tables.description: Some rows only appear when a story tag is on (war, festival) or at night. Switch the tags in the story tag list.
rows: The miller says his flour sacks are lighter every morning and he blames the owls.
A chest washed up on the riverbank last week. The bailiff took it and nobody has seen it since.
The old bridge sings when the wind comes from the east. Some say it is a warning.
A stranger has been buying every lantern in the market, and paying double.
The widow at the edge of town talks to someone at night, but she lives alone.
The baron's youngest son left home without a word and took the good horse.
Wolves have been seen in daylight, walking in a line, as if someone were leading them.
The healer in the next village has stopped taking money. People are afraid to ask why.
Salt prices doubled in a month. Somebody must be sitting on a lot of it.
The well in the square tastes of copper since the last storm.
A traveling troupe was turned away at the gate, and one of them was crying.
The ferryman refuses to cross after dark. He says the other side is closer than it was.
Someone is leaving small stone cairns along the old road, one more each day.
The priest burned a stack of papers behind the chapel and then went to bed for two days.
A farmer found a gold coin in his field, and then another one, and now he digs all day.
The hunters say the forest is quiet in a way they do not like.

rows.text: Strange lights have been seen on the hill after midnight, moving slowly in a circle.
Soldiers have been seen on the north road, more every day, and they do not stop for the toll.
The smith says he has not made a plowshare in a month, only blades and nails.
The roads are quiet and the merchants are in a good mood. Strange how nobody complains.
The baker has hidden a prize somewhere in this year's festival bread and nobody knows who will find it.

tables.name: Rumor with a teller
tables.description: A rumor and who tells it, drawn from the table of professions.
